title: Make sense of the science: three new painting ideas
lead: Mockups on the real homepage, computer and phone. Only the Mitochondria and Free radicals paintings change. The brain cell and all the words stay as they are; the one line under each painting is a suggestion.
why: Why today's paintings feel off: they are storybook drawings, not watercolors. Hard edges, heavy brown, and about ten parts in one picture (worker, boiler, wheel, belt, generator, lamp, shed, oak, hills, sky).
What the three ideas share: one object, a few wet washes, lots of bare paper, and gold leaf only where the energy is. The same hand as the mailbox and the hummingbird.

ideas.name: The lantern
ideas.say: One old barn lantern. Fuel in the base, a flame, light. Then the same lantern up close: the flame has left soot on the glass.
lines: “Like your cells: fuel goes in, and the flame turns it into light.”
“Every flame leaves a little soot. What isn’t cleared away dims the glass.”
notes: My score: 9 out of 10. The simplest and the calmest, and it reads at once on a phone.
The harm is gentle (a dimmed glass), not a burnt roof. No wildfire feeling.
The words under the paintings would change from “sparks” and “burns” to “soot”.

ideas.name: The wood stove
ideas.say: Your story, kept: fuel, fire, a screen that catches most sparks, burns from the few that slip out. Moved indoors to a cabin stove and painted as a real watercolor.
lines: “Like your cells: food is the fuel, and the fire turns it into energy.”
“Most sparks are caught. The few that slip out leave burns.” (unchanged)
notes: My score: 8.5 out of 10. The closest to what you already approved, so the fewest word changes.
The sparks and the three burns are small on a phone. A second take could make them bigger.

ideas.name: The water wheel
ideas.say: A gold-country water wheel. The stream turns the wheel, the wheel lights a lamp. Up close, the drops that stray leave rust on the iron hub.
lines: “Like your cells: food is the stream, and the wheel turns it into power.”
“Most of the water does its work. The drops that stray leave rust.”
notes: My score: 8 out of 10. The most Californian, and rust is what free radicals really do (oxidation).
The rust picture is the weakest of the six: it looks a little like a diagram. It would need another take.
No fire at all, so both lines under the paintings change.
